text.p: Canadian miner Eldorado Gold Corp is budgeting $7 million for its Argentine prospecting in 1997, the company's local exploration director said Tuesday.

Eldorado is exploring a total 300,000 hectares in northwestern Argentina, mainly at high altitude along the Chilean border, but has not yet made any discoveries, Eldorado's Ronald Robertson told Reuters.
The firm is prospecting the Laguna Verde project in Catamarca province, Rio Salado in northern La Rioja province and Pena Negra in southern La Rioja.
The prospects contain "gold, probably with some copper," Robertson said.
Much of Eldorado's Argentine exploration activity is now slowing down as the southern hemisphere winter takes grip of the mountainous sites.
Eldorado, which operates two gold mines in Mexico and one in Brazil with forecast total output of about 185,000 ounces this year, is owned 40 percent by Gencor of South Africa.
